chief_complaint: palpable purple rash over buttocks and lower legs, severe colicky abdominal pain, joint swelling, and hematuria in 6-year-old
hpi_details: 6-year-old boy post-URI with palpable purpura on the extensor legs and buttocks, ankle arthralgias, abdominal pain, and microscopic hematuria with proteinuria consistent with IgA vasculitis.
ideas: She thinks her son is having a severe allergic reaction to the cold medicine he took last week or to something he ate at school.
concerns: She is worried that the purple spots mean he has blood poisoning or that his kidneys are being permanently damaged.
expectations: She hopes the doctor will prescribe medicine for his stomach and joint pain and give him an allergy treatment to clear the rash.

available_results.value: Blood 2+, protein 1+, 20-30 red blood cells/HPF; no leukocyte esterase or nitrites

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Palpable purpura in a dependent distribution.

teaching.one_liner: 6-year-old boy post-URI with palpable purpura on legs/buttocks, colicky abdominal pain, joint swelling, and hematuria.
red_flags: Palpable purpura in a dependent distribution

must_ask.objective: Characterize the rash appearance and distribution
must_ask.say: Can you describe the rash — where is it, and does it feel raised when you touch it?
Did he have a cold or infection in the past couple of weeks?
How severe is his belly pain, and does it come and go?
Are any of his joints swollen or painful, like his ankles or knees?

must_ask.objective: Explain the need for urine monitoring
must_ask.say: We need to check his urine regularly to make sure his kidneys aren't affected.

history.answer: My 6-year-old son developed purple spots on his legs and buttocks two days ago, and now he is crying with severe tummy aches.
The purple spots first appeared on his ankles two days ago and gradually spread up his lower legs and onto his buttocks.
They are located mainly on his buttocks, the backs of his thighs, and the fronts and backs of his lower legs on both sides.
They look like raised, reddish-purple raised bumps and small blotches that feel slightly bumpy when you touch them.
He does not complain of itching or burning, but he says his ankles and legs ache.
No, the spots stay in the same place and do not disappear or move around throughout the day.
No, he has never had purple spots or anything like this before.
He does not have a fever right now, though he feels tired and wants to lie down because of his belly and legs.
No, I looked inside his mouth and eyes, and there are no sores, ulcers, redness, or blisters.
When I press on the purple bumps, the color does not fade at all, and his skin is not peeling.
No, his lips, face, and tongue look completely normal, and he is breathing easily without any wheezing.
No, he has not started any new prescription medications, antibiotics, or painkillers recently.
No new foods, detergents, soaps, body washes, or metal jewelry have been introduced at home.
He has not been bitten by ticks or bugs, and we haven't visited any woods, hiking trails, or public pools.
Nobody else at home or in his kindergarten has had a rash like this.
He has no history of atopic dermatitis, asthma, or allergic rhinitis.
I put a little moisturizing lotion on his legs, but I haven't applied any steroid or antifungal creams.
He had a mild cold with a runny nose and cough about ten days ago, but that resolved on its own after three or four days.
The pain is around his belly button and comes in sharp, crampy waves that make him curl up in bed.
He hasn't vomited, and he had a normal soft brown stool yesterday without any visible red blood or black tarry material.
Both of his ankles look puffy and swollen, and it hurts so much that he refuses to walk on them today.
His urine looked slightly darker than usual this morning, almost like iced tea, but he didn't complain of any burning when peeing.
I thought maybe he was having an allergic reaction to the cough medicine we gave him last week or to something he touched at school.
I'm terrified that the purple spots mean he has blood poisoning or that his kidneys are failing because of the dark urine.
I'm hoping you can give him medicine to ease his belly and leg pain, and something to make this awful rash go away.
He has always been a healthy boy with no chronic health conditions.
He has never had any surgeries and has never been admitted to a hospital.
He does not take any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or vitamin supplements.
He has no known allergies to medicines, foods, or environmental triggers.
No one in our family smokes, and he is never exposed to tobacco smoke.
He lives in an apartment with me, his father, and his older sister.
There is no family history of kidney disorders, bleeding diseases, or autoimmune conditions.
He was born at full term via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery with no newborn complications.
His childhood immunizations are fully up to date, and his growth and milestones have all been completely normal.
He attends a local kindergarten classroom, and none of his classmates are currently sick.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 105/65 mmHg, heart rate 98 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, body temperature 37.1 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert 6-year-old boy in mild distress due to intermittent crampy abdominal pain, lying still on the examination bed.

Multiple non-blanching palpable erythematous-to-purpuric papules and plaques distributed symmetrically over the buttocks, posterior thighs, and extensor surfaces of the lower legs, with normal nails, scalp, and web spaces.
Pink and moist oral mucosa without petechiae, aphthous ulcers, or tonsillar exudates.
Clear sclerae without jaundice and pink conjunctivae without pallor or injection.
No palpable cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Normal bowel sounds present throughout all four quadrants without bruits.
Soft abdomen with moderate diffuse periumbilical tenderness, but no palpable mass, organomegaly, or involuntary guarding.
No rebound tenderness across the abdomen.
Bilateral ankle swelling with mild warmth and tenderness, associated with painful limitation of active motion, but no knee or wrist effusion.
No costovertebral angle tenderness on either side.
